## 1. What this application is

`u2giants/shared-db` is the canonical repository for **one** Supabase PostgreSQL database shared by five separate applications, each in its own repo:

| App | What it is | Status | Repo |
|---|---|---|---|
| PopDAM | digital asset management | live | `u2giants/popdam3` |
| PopCRM | customer relationship management | live | `u2giants/popcrm-web` |
| DesignFlow PLM ("dflow") | product lifecycle management | live | `popcre/designflow-*` (six repos) |
| PopPIM | product information management | in development | `u2giants/poppim-web` |
| monitor | Synology NAS monitoring | live | `u2giants/synology-monitor` |

Every schema/DDL change is authored **here**, proved on the **preview** database (project `rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel`), then promoted to **production** (project `qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`). There is no "just my app" change — one bad migration breaks all five, and it is normally found days later by a user rather than by a test.

**Who works here:** AI sessions (Claude, Codex, GLM, Grok, Kimi, Qwen), frequently **3–7 at once**, across several machines, sometimes **in the same working copy**. The owner, **Albert Hazan**, is a business owner and **explicitly not a programmer** — AI sessions are the entire engineering department. **Controls must be mechanical; anything that relies on a human remembering a written rule will not happen.** That single fact drives every design decision in this workstream.

**Branch model:** branch + PR, and **the AI merges its own PRs.** This is specific to `shared-db`; do NOT self-merge in the dflow repos.

**Stack relevant to this work:** plain Node.js ESM scripts under `scripts/`. No build step, no framework, no `npm install`. Tests are `node --test`. **Nothing in this workstream touches the database at all.**

## 2. What we set out to do this session, and why

**In business terms:** stop two AI agents being sent to change the same part of the database at the same time — *before* either does the work, so nobody's work is thrown away.

**The specific technical objective this session:** execute **Phase A** of `plan_dispatch-collision-hardening.md` and nothing else. I was told explicitly not to start Phase B in the same session, and I did not.

**What triggered it.** A tool built the previous day (`scripts/check-dispatch-collision.mjs`, PR #464) printed a confident, wrong answer in the most common case:

```
# An open PR already contains:  alter table core.licensor add column risk_tier text;
node scripts/check-dispatch-collision.mjs --task "agent B" --objects "table core.licensor"
  → SAFE TO DISPATCH — no in-flight work touches these objects.        exit 0
```

That is false. The SQL parser it reuses models only `function`, `procedure`, `view`, `materialized view`, `trigger` and `policy`, in `create`/`drop` forms only. It has **no `alter` verb of any kind** — measured **754 modelled statements versus 1,921 unmodelled** across `supabase/migrations/`.

**The governing rule for this whole workstream, from the plan §1 — it outranks the plan's own steps:** *if a change would make the tool more likely to print a confident answer it cannot justify, do not make it, even if the plan says to. A tool that says "I could not tell" is correct; a tool that says "safe" when it did not look is the bug.*

## 4. Everything we tried that did NOT work

**My predecessor's §4 lists twelve dead ends and they all still apply — read that file, do not re-derive them.** The highlights you must not repeat: a plain `git push` is **not** a create-only lock (a descendant commit silently steals it); GitHub does **not** refuse `refs/db-claims/*`; a database registry table is rejected; check-then-claim is a race; the claim mini-language produced four defects in a day.

**New to THIS session:**

1. **Landing step 2's red tests as ordinary failing tests — impossible, and the plan's instruction could not be followed literally.** The plan says *"run them red locally and land them together with the step-3 fix so the mergeable tip is green."* That works only if steps 2 and 3 are in the **same phase**. They are not: step 2 is Phase A and step 3b is Phase B, and I was instructed not to start Phase B. A PR whose tip is red can never merge past the **required** `Cross-PR object collision` job, so landing them red would have stranded Phase A permanently.
   **What I did instead:** landed them with `node --test`'s `{ todo: … }` option. They still run, they still fail, and `node --test` reports `ℹ todo 4` on **every** run, so the gap stays visible — but they do not fail the build. **This is a deliberate, temporary state and step 3b must remove it.** I did not use `skip`, because a skipped test is invisible and that would have been exactly the silent-failure pattern this repo forbids.

2. **Asserting the report contains no `/safe/i` — my first wording failed my own test.** I wrote the empty-in-flight line as *"That is a statement about the inputs, not about safety."* The word **safety** contains **safe**, so the "no verdict word anywhere" test went red. Rewritten to *"not a clearance."* Trivial, but it proves the test is doing real work — keep that assertion, and do not reintroduce the word in any branch of the output.

3. **Backticks inside the `USAGE` template literal — a syntax error that killed the whole module.** `USAGE` is a JavaScript template literal (backtick-delimited). I wrote the exit-code documentation using Markdown-style `` `alter table` `` quoting inside it, which terminated the literal and produced `SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'alter'` — the module would not even load, so every test in both suites failed at once. **Use double quotes inside `USAGE`, never backticks.**

4. **`bash bin/ai-install-skills` (in `ai-devops`) — does not run on this machine.** It dies at `set -o pipefail` with `invalid option name`, because the file has CRLF line endings and Git Bash on Windows chokes on them. Same root cause defeats `bash scripts/check-sql.sh` locally. **I did not "fix" either script** — the line endings are the issue, backlog item **B1** owns them, and editing the scripts would be a band-aid that also fights CI (which runs them fine on Linux). **Workaround used:** copied the skill file directly to `C:\Users\ahazan2\.claude\skills\shared-db-orchestrator\SKILL.md` and verified with `Get-FileHash` that hub and local are identical.

5. **Deferring the AGENTS.md / skill fix to plan step 8 — considered and rejected.** Step 8 (Phase C) owns those documents, so leaving them was "in scope discipline." But step 1b made the exact command they publish exit 2, which would have broken the dispatch gate for every coordinator across two whole phases. Shipping a known-broken instruction to preserve a phase boundary is the wrong trade. Corrected both now, and recorded it as drift D-A7 so step 8 knows what is already done and what it still owes.

6. **Leaving `claimCommand`'s bash heredoc silently broken — rejected; labelled instead.** Decision D18 forbids a printed heredoc (this is a PowerShell-first machine, which is *part of why zero claims have ever been filed*). ## 5. Root causes and key findings

**A. The finding that matters most for Phase B, restated because it is easy to lose:** before this session, **every** test in `check-dispatch-collision.test.mjs` injected object arrays by hand. **If `extractObjects` had returned `[]` for every input, the entire 23-test suite would still have passed.** That is how a parser blind to the dominant DDL class shipped behind a green build. The four new tests close it — but only once step 3b makes them pass.

**B. The positive control is why those four failures are trustworthy.** A red test proves *something* is wrong, not *what*. The fifth test (`create or replace function` → `['function plm.promote_coldlion_source_owned']` → collision detected) passes, which proves the extract→compare wiring is sound and isolates the failure to the parser's vocabulary. **Keep it. If step 3b ever makes the control fail, the wiring broke, not the patterns.**

**C. Renaming a printed string is not a fix — and the test now enforces that.** The old meaning lived in three places besides the sentence: the field `result.safe`, the `USAGE` gloss, and the exit code. A test asserts the result object has **no key named `safe`**, so a future session cannot quietly restore the old semantics for `--json` consumers while leaving the new wording in place.

**D. The gatherer defects were untestable by construction, and that is the real lesson.** `gatherOpenPrObjects` called `gh` inline, so none of its five defects could be unit tested without a network. I split the three GitHub calls into an injectable object, `defaultIo` (`:433`), exported for tests: `{listPulls, listPullFiles, readFileAtRef}`. All five defects now have a test. **Any new gathering added in step 5 must go through the same object or its defects become untestable too.**

**E. `encodeURI` vs `encodeURIComponent` is not a style choice.** `encodeURI` leaves `#` alone, so a migration path containing one truncates at the fragment, the file reads as empty, and that PR's DDL silently vanishes from the comparison — a false clear. The sibling merge guard uses `encodeURI` at `check-pr-object-collisions.mjs:393,428`; **do not copy it here.** `encodeRepoPath` encodes each segment with `encodeURIComponent` and rejoins with `/`.

**F. The two ref lifetimes, repeated because confusing them freezes the schema.** **Version refs → kept permanently** (plan D13; the preview ledger is persistent, so reusing a number can collide with something preview already recorded). **Object refs → always released** (plan D16; never releasing one locks that object forever). Partial acquisition therefore needs rollback for *object* refs even though rollback was rejected for *version* refs.

**G. The shared-checkout hazard did NOT bite this session, and here is why.** `C:\repos\shared-db` is shared with other live sessions. Before opening the PR I ran `git diff origin/main --stat` and confirmed it listed **only** the five files I meant to change. I staged explicit paths, never `git add -A`. **Do the same.** (My predecessor's session was not so lucky — its branch silently inherited another session's commit `48680a3`, which later reached `main` by another route along with a commit that *retracted* the claim it made.)

## 6. Exact next steps

**Phase B. Start at step 3a. The authoritative detail is in the plan; this is the ordered summary with gates.**

### ⚠️ Before you write a single line

Read **plan §14 "DRIFT AFTER PHASE A"** (ten items, D-A1 … D-A10). It is not background — it lists the function signatures, field names and file positions that Phase A changed and that steps 3a–8 all assume. **D-A10 in particular: every line number inside the plan's step bodies (§9) is now wrong by 20–60 lines.** The refreshed table in plan §5 is the one to trust; better still, grep for the symbol name, which is stable.

1. **Step 3a — the historical noise gate. DO THIS FIRST; it is a gate, not a risk note.**
   Broadening the parser also strengthens `check-pr-object-collisions.mjs`, a **required** check on `main`. If concurrent PRs routinely touch the same table, that check becomes noisy — which is the alarm-fatigue disease this whole workstream exists to cure.
   Reconstruct sets of PRs that were **open at the same time** (from `gh pr list --state merged` with created/merged timestamps) — *not* "the last ten PRs in isolation"; overlap is the only thing that matters. Run the proposed extraction and policies over those sets, classify every new failure as **useful / harmless-but-worth-serializing / noise**, and **fix the acceptance rule BEFORE you look at the results** (suggested: >20% of concurrent sets producing a new merge-guard failure classified as noise ⇒ the merge guard keeps its narrow policy and only the dispatch policy broadens).
   *You'll know it worked when:* a written artefact exists under `docs/verification/` recording the sets tested, the pre-registered rule, the classification and the decision. **That artefact is the evidence for decision D12 and must exist before step 3b merges.**

2. **Step 3b — structured operations, and two policies over one parser.**
   The parser returns `{action, kind, target}` objects (`extractOperations`), and each consumer applies its own policy: dispatch = any write to the same target collides (broad, fails safe); merge guard = keeps its current narrow behaviour unless 3a's evidence says widen. **Do not collapse this into one flat shared list** — that was rejected as R7.
   Watch the specifics the plan calls out: `GRANT` can target sequences/schemas/functions, `COMMENT ON COLUMN core.t.c` must collide with `core.t`, `ALTER POLICY n ON t` needs both identities, `RENAME`/`SET SCHEMA` need old and new, `CREATE INDEX` emits index *and* table. Start **table-level** granularity (D9). Reuse `normalizeSql` and **do not change its deliberately non-`$`-anchored line-comment regex** (its header explains why).
   **Three things from Phase A you must honour here:**
   - `extractObjects` stays as the flat-string wrapper, and it must flatten **every** operation including the new kinds — otherwise the four step-2 tests stay red forever (drift D-A6).
   - New kinds must use the **same words as `KNOWN_DDL_CLASSES`** (`table`, `column`, `index`, `grant`, `comment`, `type`, `sequence`, `schema`). A different word (`tables`, `indexes`) leaves the class on the printed NOT CHECKED list forever (drift D-A4).
   - **Delete the `TODO_UNTIL_STEP_3B` option from all four step-2 tests** (drift D-A5).
   Add the **coverage-inventory test** the plan asks for: scan `supabase/migrations/` for leading DDL verbs, subtract what the parser models, fail if any unmodelled verb exceeds a threshold. That is what prevents a repeat of this entire defect.
   *You'll know it worked when:* the four tests pass **without** a `todo` marker; the positive control still passes; `node --test scripts/check-pr-object-collisions.test.mjs` stays green; and
   `node -e 'import("./scripts/check-pr-object-collisions.mjs").then(m=>console.log(m.extractObjects("alter table core.licensor add column foo text;")))'` prints `[ 'table core.licensor' ]`.

3. **Step 4 — make `--sql` the primary input.** Derive objects from a draft migration where one exists; when `--objects` is used without `--sql`, print a one-line note that the list is unverified. **Do not remove `--objects`** — at genuine dispatch time the SQL does not exist yet, which is the entire point.
   *You'll know it worked when:* `--sql <a real file from supabase/migrations/>` lists that migration's tables and functions.

4. **Step 5 — `--claim`: acquire object refs atomically. THE CORE CHANGE.**
   One object = one ref. `POST /repos/u2giants/shared-db/git/refs` on `refs/db-claims/objects/<kind>/<key>` succeeds or returns `422 Reference already exists`. **Acquisition IS the check** (D17) — there is no check-then-claim step, so the time-of-check/time-of-use race and self-collision both vanish. Ref names must be deterministic **and injective**: percent-encode anything outside `[a-z0-9._/-]`, and **if sanitising changed the key at all, append `--<first 8 hex of sha256(canonical key)>`**. Acquire in sorted order; on the first 422, **release everything already acquired in this attempt** and exit 1. Open PRs are still consulted, because refs only cover work that claimed. Delete `claimCommand` and `bodyFromClaimCommand` and their tests.
   *You'll know it worked when:* claim a test object (exit 0), claim it again from a second invocation (exit 1, naming the holder), release it, and `gh api repos/u2giants/shared-db/git/matching-refs/db-claims/objects --jq '.[].ref'` returns empty.

5. **Step 5b — release object refs on merge, and define staleness.** A `push: branches: [main]` workflow that deletes the matching object refs for every migration in the merged commit. Staleness reads the ref's target commit: ancestor of `origin/main` ⇒ merged, release; on no open PR and no remote branch ⇒ abandoned, release; otherwise live, leave it.
   *You'll know it worked when:* a PR carrying a claimed migration merges and the ref disappears with nobody running a command.

6. **Step 6 — `--reserve-version`.** Atomic create-if-absent via the same REST endpoint; on 422 increment and retry (bounded). **Never `git push`** (R3). Refs kept **permanently** — no release, no rollback, no reconciliation (R8/R9). Name it `--reserve-version`, not `--allocate-version`, because it mutates remote state. **Recommendation: keep `--allocate-version` permanently as the exit-2 tombstone** rather than deleting the flag, so an older pasted command gets the explanation instead of `unknown argument` (drift D-A9).
   *You'll know it worked when:* reserving the same test version twice fails the second time with 422, and every test ref is deleted afterwards.

7. **Step 8 — the documents.** Partly done already (drift D-A7). **Still owed:** the `AGENTS.md` "KNOWN LIMIT" paragraph (rewrite once the parser can see the classes it currently names), the step-6 reservation and release commands, and the same in `skills/claude/shared-db-orchestrator/SKILL.md` in **`u2giants/ai-devops`** (a different repo at `C:\repos\ai-devops`, main-only, push directly, no PR).
   *You'll know it worked when:* the hub file and `C:\Users\ahazan2\.claude\skills\shared-db-orchestrator\SKILL.md` are identical (compare hashes — `bin/ai-install-skills` does not run on this machine, see §4.4), and `SAFE TO DISPATCH` appears in neither document.

## 7. Constraints and gotchas in force

1. **Branch + PR; you merge it yourself.** Never commit to `main` directly. Specific to `shared-db`.
2. **Commit identity must be `Albert Hazan <u2giants@users.noreply.github.com>`.** Check `git var GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT` **before** your first commit — 231 wrong-identity commits already reached shared branches and cannot be fixed.
3. **No database contact is needed for any step in this plan.** No migration, no preview/production push, no `supabase` CLI, no Supabase MCP, no `psql`. If you find yourself needing one, stop — something has gone wrong.
4. **Branch protection: `strict: true`, six required contexts, `enforce_admins: true`.** Your branch must be up to date before merging. Verify with `gh api repos/u2giants/shared-db/branches/main/protection --jq '{strict:.required_status_checks.strict, contexts:.required_status_checks.contexts}'`. **Do not turn `strict` back off** — it was enabled 2026-08-06 at Albert's explicit instruction and the collision guard's own header depends on it.
5. **Never rename the CI job `Cross-PR object collision`** — it is a required status context, and renaming it makes every future PR hang forever waiting for a check that never reports.
6. **Never weaken `check-pr-object-collisions.mjs`'s `Skip`-to-green posture.** A *required* gate that cannot gather its inputs must warn and pass, or it blocks every PR. The dispatch tool's opposite posture (unknown ⇒ exit 2) is also deliberate. **Do not "harmonise" them.**
7. **No band-aids, no silent failures.** Every fallback must be loud. This is why `todo` was used rather than `skip`, and why an empty file body throws.
8. **`shared-db` is a PUBLIC repo.** Do not create issues, labels, or other public content without asking Albert.
9. **Clean up every test ref you create.** Verify with `gh api repos/u2giants/shared-db/git/matching-refs/db-claims --jq '.[].ref'` returning empty.
10. **You may be sharing this checkout with another live session.** Before opening a PR, run `git diff origin/main --stat` and confirm it lists **only** files you meant to change. Never `git add -A`; stage explicit paths. **Uncommitted changes you did not make are another session's live work — leave them.**
11. **Do not delete `.ai/deepseek-sessions/` or `.ai/reviews/`** — untracked, not yours.
12. **Windows line endings.** `.mjs` edits show a `LF will be replaced by CRLF` warning. Harmless; do not "fix" it and do not reformat whole files (backlog B1 owns `.gitattributes`).
13. **Backticks are illegal inside the `USAGE` template literal.** See §4.3 — it is a syntax error that breaks the entire module.
14. **`COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md` blocks are moved only by the coordinator**, and only forward.
15. **The stranded-CI-run trap.** During a GitHub Actions outage a required check can be left at `status=queued, conclusion=null` for hours; GitHub refuses to cancel it while still reporting it queued, so the PR stays BLOCKED forever. `gh run rerun` does not help and closing/reopening the PR does not help — **only moving the SHA does**: `git commit --allow-empty -m "ci: re-trigger checks stranded by an Actions outage" && git push`. Diagnose with `gh api repos/u2giants/shared-db/actions/runs/<id> --jq '.status, .conclusion, .updated_at'` — a `queued` run whose `updated_at` is hours old is stranded, not slow. (Did not occur this session; CI was healthy and finished in about 90 seconds.)

- **Other models available for review** (all read-only; the wrappers own the model pin and permissions): `C:/repos/ai-devops/bin/ai-grok-review` (not on PATH — use the absolute path), `ai-glm`, `codex exec`, `kimi`. ⚠️ **Codex must run at `low` or `medium` reasoning effort only — never `high` or `none`.** Pass `-c model_reasoning_effort='medium'` explicitly and read the header line it prints.
- **Secrets:** none are needed for this plan. If one ever is, it is in **1Password vault `vibe_coding`**, referenced by item title or ID — **never paste a value into a file, doc, commit, or chat.**

## 9. Open questions, risks, and decisions

### Open (decide before the relevant step)

1. **D8 — ref namespace:** `refs/db-claims/*` or `refs/heads/db-claims/*`? Both verified working live. Recommendation: the former, since it is invisible in the branch list and cannot add to the ~131-branch clutter. Implementer's call, in step 5.
2. **D9 — granularity:** table-level vs column-level object keys. **Start table-level** — it over-blocks, which fails safe.
3. **D10 — staleness for optional claim *issues*.** Object *refs* get their own rule in step 5b; D10 stays open only if optional claim issues are used at all.
4. **The enforcement CI check** (fail a migration PR with no covering claim) is deliberately deferred (R4). Kimi's sequencing argument: ship the gate before the compliant path is cheap and you get pressure for an exemption label, which becomes the norm and kills the gate. **Build the scaffold tool and auto-draft bot first.**
5. **Albert has not decided** whether to migrate `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md` (~4,500 lines, 63 open items) to GitHub Issues. Recommended by all three external reviewers; not started.

### Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| **Broadening the parser makes the *required* merge guard stricter and retro-fails PRs that used to pass** — the highest-impact risk in this plan | Step 3a is a hard gate: reconstruct *concurrently-open* PR sets, classify new failures, and **fix the acceptance rule before seeing results** |
| **Step 3b lands and nobody removes the four `todo` markers** — the fix would then be unproven while looking done | Called out in the plan STATUS table, in plan §14 D-A5, in the test file's own comment block, and in §6 above |
| Someone "simplifies" object claiming back to check-then-claim, or the lock back to `git push` | Plan R11 and R3 record the live test results that killed both |
| Object refs never released ⇒ that object is frozen forever | Step 5b; and §5F above |
| Another session's work is swept into your branch | §5G, §7.10 |

- **2026-08-07 — the repo's `.sh` scripts were NOT edited** to work around Windows CRLF. Backlog B1 owns that. §4.4.

## Self-audit (mandatory gate — completed before this handoff was shown)

**1. Could a brand-new developer with no project knowledge pick up where I left off and not skip a beat?** **Yes.** §1 defines the five dependent apps, the two database projects, the branch model, the stack and who works here. §3 gives the merged SHA, the PR, the exact state of all four Phase A steps with `file:line`, and the commands that verified each. §6 gives ordered steps with a verification gate each, and states plainly that Phase B starts at **3a, not 3b** — the single most likely mistake. §8 covers CLIs, Node versions and the shell trap. *Gap found during the audit and fixed:* the first draft sent the reader to the plan without saying that the plan's own line numbers are now wrong; §6's preamble and plan §14 D-A10 now say it explicitly, because a reader trusting `main() around lines 425–440` would edit the wrong place.

**2. Could they continue as effectively as I can right now?** **Yes.** §4 records six new dead ends including three where the plan's literal instruction could not be followed (`todo` vs red tests, the AGENTS.md deferral, the heredoc) and two self-inflicted failures with their exact error text (the `safety`/`safe` collision, the backtick syntax error). §5 records the five findings that cost real time, each with the `file:line` that settles it. §9 dates every decision so a later session cannot unknowingly contradict one. *Gap found and fixed:* the first draft explained the `todo` markers only in §4; because forgetting to remove them would leave the workstream's central defect shipping behind a green build, it is now stated in **four** places — §3, §4.1, §6 step 2, and the risk table.

**3. Is every detail needed for flawless execution included?** **Yes.** Background (§1–2), current state with SHAs and verification output (§3), failures (§4), findings (§5), exact next actions with gates (§6), constraints including the CI-stranding trap and the shared-checkout rule (§7), access (§8), risks and dated decisions (§9), plus the explicit N/A for sub-agents. Secrets are referenced by vault only. *Gap found and fixed:* the first draft omitted that `HANDOFF.d/` is over the file-count threshold and that the root `HANDOFF.md` is un-migrated — both are things a newcomer would otherwise trip over on their very first action, so a Housekeeping section was added.

**Checklist:** all 9 sections present · part (b) explicitly N/A with reason · a newcomer could proceed without asking a question · dead ends included with why they failed · every next step carries a "you'll know it worked when" gate · every SHA, path, flag and identifier defined · commit/push/merge status explicit for each piece of work · no secret values. **All items pass.**
